c.tagline: Windswept Patagonian port on Last Hope Sound, the launchpad for Torres del Paine.

taxi.fareNote: Standard taxis are black with a yellow roof and metered; shared 'colectivos' run fixed routes for a low flat per-person fare. There are no ride-hailing apps (no Uber) in Puerto Natales, so hail a taxi on the street or book by phone or through your hotel.

emergency.note: 133 reaches Carabineros (police), 131 the SAMU ambulance service, and 132 the fire brigade; 112 also works from mobile phones.

hood_landmark.Centro (Plaza de Armas): Plaza de Armas Puerto Natales church
hood_landmark.Costanera (Última Esperanza waterfront): Costanera Puerto Natales Última Esperanza Sound Milodón sculpture
hood_landmark.Sector Norte (Ruta 9): Ruta 9 Puerto Natales road to Torres del Paine

hood_desc: The compact grid heart of town around the Plaza de Armas and its church, lined with trekking-gear shops, cafes, breweries and tour agencies; best for first-timers who want to organise a Torres del Paine trip with everything a short walk away.

The windswept waterfront promenade along Última Esperanza (Last Hope) Sound, with the town's best fjord-and-mountain views, the Milodón monument and a string of hotels and seafood restaurants; suits travelers who want scenery and sunsets on the doorstep.
A quiet residential grid just back from the water, full of colourful corrugated-metal houses, family guesthouses and B&Bs; good value and local, a few blocks' walk from the centre and the shore.

A historic hamlet about 5 km north where a huge early-1900s sheep-processing plant (frigorífico) has been reborn as a landmark hotel and museum; calm, scenic and upmarket, right on the sound away from town bustle.

The northern edge of town where Ruta 9 heads out toward Torres del Paine, with larger hotels, cabañas and the trailhead up Cerro Dorotea; practical for drivers and early park departures, quieter and more spread out.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.pay: Pay the driver in cash (Chilean pesos); colectivos charge a low flat per-person fare and taxis are metered or agreed first. There is no rechargeable transit card.
transit.hours: Colectivos and micros run roughly 8:00 AM to about 9-10:00 PM, with reduced service on Sundays; taxis and hotel transfers fill the late-night and pre-dawn trekking-departure gaps.
transit.note: Puerto Natales is small enough to cross on foot in 20-30 minutes and has no metro or rail; getting around means shared-route taxi colectivos, a few local micros, and regular taxis, plus the long-distance bus terminal and trekking shuttles out to Torres del Paine. There are no ride-hailing apps.

air: Presidente Carlos Ibáñez del Campo International Airport, Punta Arenas (PUQ)
bus: Rodoviario bus terminal - Bus-Sur, Buses Fernández, Buses Pacheco
Vans & shuttles to Torres del Paine (Laguna Amarga, Pudeto, Administración)

car.idp: Recommended (carry an IDP with your national license)

ferry: Navimag ferry from/to Puerto Montt through the fjords
Boat trips on Última Esperanza Sound to the Serrano & Balmaceda glaciers

transit.m: Taxi to the town centre, ~10-15 min
Bus/van transfer from Punta Arenas airport (PUQ), ~3 hr, for the many visitors who fly there instead

tip.r: 10% is customary at restaurants and often suggested on the bill (propina sugerida); rounding up for taxis is optional.
